title: Smoked Queso Fundido
shortDescription: Melted cheese dip with chorizo finished on the smoker for ten
subtitle: Melted cheese dip with chorizo finished on the smoker for ten
description: Chorizo is browned, combined with a blend of melting cheeses and roasted peppers, then finished in a cast-iron skillet on the smoker until bubbling and lightly smoke-kissed. Tortilla chips and warm flour tortillas complete the spread.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Smoked Queso Fundido in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Double-check seasoning after scaling — crew palates run salty after long shifts, so taste the first portion before opening the line.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch pork. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Brown the chorizo
steps.instruction: Cook crumbled chorizo in a skillet over medium heat until fully browned and fat renders, about 8 minutes. Drain excess fat, leaving just enough to coat the pan.

steps.title: Sweat aromatics
steps.instruction: Add diced onion and garlic to the chorizo fat and cook until softened and translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in roasted poblano peppers and remove from direct heat.

steps.title: Build the cheese base
steps.instruction: Fold in cream cheese until melted, then gradually add Oaxaca, Monterey Jack, and heavy cream, stirring until the mixture is smooth and evenly combined.

steps.title: Smoke until bubbling
steps.instruction: Transfer skillet to smoker at 275°F and smoke uncovered 25–30 minutes until surface bubbles, edges brown lightly, and center reaches 165°F for safe holding. Target oven/smoker temperature: 275°F.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F with a 3-minute rest. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Smoked Queso Fundido onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 10 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Serve immediately
steps.instruction: Place hot skillet on a trivet with chips and warm tortillas around the board. Replenish chips as needed and keep backup queso warm at 170°F in a crock if the first batch disappears fast.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Smoked Queso Fundido — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: A tablespoon of cornstarch whisked into the cream helps queso stay emulsified during long holds.
Add diced tomatoes only after smoking so they stay fresh, not mushy.
For extra smoke, put a small foil pouch of wood chips directly on the burner side of a pellet grill.
tonightSpread: Smoking-hot queso skillet with chips, tortillas, pickled jalapeños, and lime wedges.
Simple black bean salad with cilantro for a fresh counterpoint to the rich cheese.
leftovers: Reheat gently with a splash of milk and serve over grilled chicken rice bowls.
Spread cold queso on flour tortillas and griddle into crispy quesadillas for lunch.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Queso fundido is built for grazing while watching the game or debriefing after a call. Smoking the skillet adds depth that stovetop-only versions miss, and the format scales to a hungry hall.
mealPrepNotes: Brown chorizo ahead and refrigerate. Shred cheese into labeled bags. Assemble cold in the skillet and smoke from chilled, adding 10 minutes to the cook time.
